reason: The text depicts the plagues of Egypt (Exodus 8-10) and makes distinctions between groups, but not based on inherent superiority of elites. Rather, the distinctions are based on divine covenant and God's will: the Israelites (presented as enslaved people, not an elite class) are protected in Goshen through God's intervention, while Egypt's elite—Pharaoh and his magicians (חרטומים)—are depicted as failing and overcome by the plagues. The magicians specifically cannot stand before Moses due to boils (וְלֹֽא־ יָכְל֣וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֗ים לַעֲמֹ֛ד). The text emphasizes God's power and covenant choice, not any inherent superiority of the elite class. In fact, the narrative suggests the opposite: the elite's power and authority are shown to be ineffective against divine will.
